source_user: Advanced cluster case cluster scheduling and recovery-116: Design a resilient cluster scheduler for distributed LLM training and inference. Variant 116 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: cover gang scheduling, GPU/NIC/topology-aware placement, fragmentation, preemption, checkpoint cadence, node drain, elastic restart, replica routing, SLOs, and resource accounting. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: the scheduler controls heterogeneous multi-node GPU jobs and inference replicas, while device, fabric, firmware, and workload details must be measured rather than assumed. Hypothesis: topology-aware gang admission plus checkpoint-safe recovery will improve deadline-compliant throughput and recovery time without violating isolation or increasing tail latency; this is falsifiable against a matched topology-blind baseline.

Design and mechanism: represent each job as a gang with GPU, CPU, memory, local NVMe, RDMA NIC, and topology constraints. Admit only when the whole gang can be placed, score candidates by free capacity and GPU/NIC/NUMA/RDMA/NVLink locality, and report fragmentation separately from raw utilization. Reserve headroom for control-plane and recovery capacity. For inference, use readiness-gated replicas, bounded queues, load-aware routing, and drain-before-termination; do not send traffic to a replica until health, model version, and connectivity checks pass. Preempt only checkpointable work under an explicit priority/fair-share policy, charge reserved and actual resources separately, and protect critical control-plane capacity.

Failure and recovery: checkpoint at a measured cadence (including checkpoint duration and storage bandwidth), use versioned, integrity-checked checkpoints, and make restart idempotent. On node or fabric fault, fence the suspect node before rescheduling, drain healthy work where safe, record the failed rank and topology, and restart with bounded backoff and an operator-visible retry budget. Elastic restart must define minimum/maximum world size, optimizer-state semantics, and when to fail closed rather than silently change training behavior. Roll back admission, placement, or routing changes if checkpoint corruption, repeated fencing, error-budget burn, isolation violations, or deadline/tail-latency SLO breach occurs.

Measurement plan: log scheduler decision and queue/admission times, gang wait, placement fragmentation, GPU/NIC/NUMA locality, allocated versus consumed resources, preemption/checkpoint overhead, restart and time-to-recovery, job completion/deadline rate, training throughput (samples/s or tokens/s), inference p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), goodput, error rate, and RDMA/NVLink retransmits or link errors with units. Compare randomized or time-matched workloads against a topology-blind and recovery-baseline policy, stratified by job size and fault type, with synchronized clocks and confidence intervals. Control for model, batch/sequence length, world size, driver/firmware, topology, background load, cache state, and fault injection; verify rollback with a canary and least-privilege, auditable changes. Treat any unmeasured platform behavior as evidence_required, not as a claimed improvement.\n\nTask-specific emphasis: For implementation, expose dry-run placement and admission decisions, emit structured events, and test fencing, retry, and authorization paths without contacting production.
risks: Topology, failure semantics, and SLO thresholds are deployment-specific and must be measured.
Aggressive preemption or elastic resizing can lose work or change training semantics.
Fault injection and scheduler changes can affect production availability if isolation and rollback gates are absent.
evidence_required: Matched baseline runs with documented topology, workload, units, and synchronized timestamps.
Fault-injection results for node, NIC/RDMA, checkpoint, and control-plane failures.
Canary and rollback evidence plus audit logs and least-privilege authorization review.

Control for model, batch/sequence length, world size, driver/firmware, topology, background load, cache state, and fault injection; verify rollback with a canary and least-privilege, auditable changes. Treat any unmeasured platform behavior as evidence_required, not as a claimed improvement.\n\nTask-specific emphasis: Separate scheduler state, placement, checkpoint metadata, and routing control; use durable leases and explicit ownership to avoid split brain.
risks: Topology, failure semantics, and SLO thresholds are deployment-specific and must be measured.
Aggressive preemption or elastic resizing can lose work or change training semantics.
Fault injection and scheduler changes can affect production availability if isolation and rollback gates are absent.
evidence_required: Matched baseline runs with documented topology, workload, units, and synchronized timestamps.
Fault-injection results for node, NIC/RDMA, checkpoint, and control-plane failures.
Canary and rollback evidence plus audit logs and least-privilege authorization review.
